none: do not imply any formal approval step is blocking this
finance_approval: the requester may mention budget codes, reimbursement, PO, purchasing, or payment details without naming a formal step
the requester may ask whether any spend or billing information is still missing
manager_approval: the requester may mention they already checked with their manager or are unsure who still needs to reply
the requester may sound like they do not understand why this has not moved forward through reviews yet
multi_step_approval: the requester may feel like this keeps stalling or bouncing around between handoffs
the requester may hint that multiple checks seem involved without naming internal approver chains
security_approval: the requester may mention extra access restrictions or checks without sounding like they know the internal process
the requester may say role or group access still is not available even after the usual request steps

COMPLETENESS_GUIDANCE.complete: include enough detail for the issue to feel concrete
COMPLETENESS_GUIDANCE.minimal: make it noticeably vague or incomplete
COMPLETENESS_GUIDANCE.partial: leave out one concrete detail a resolver would likely ask for, such as date, amount, ID, or system context

none: the requester expects this should be a fairly straightforward fix or answer
waiting_for_another_team: the requester may say one part was already handled elsewhere but the problem is still unresolved
the requester may describe being redirected before without calling out internal ownership
waiting_for_document: the requester may mention they already uploaded something or ask what information is still missing
the requester may refer to a form, receipt, contract, or tax document without spelling out the full process
waiting_for_manager: the requester may say they already followed up internally and still do not know what else is needed
the requester may hint that someone on their side might still need to respond
waiting_for_system_sync: the requester may describe that something was changed already but the tool still shows the old state or membership
the requester may point out that the update does not seem to have taken effect yet
waiting_for_vendor: the requester may say outside information is still missing or incomplete
the requester may mention waiting on details from an external contact

EMOTION_GUIDANCE.apologetic: sound a little apologetic or hesitant
EMOTION_GUIDANCE.confused: let the tone reflect uncertainty and mild confusion
EMOTION_GUIDANCE.frustrated: sound frustrated but still normal and believable for workplace ticket language
EMOTION_GUIDANCE.neutral: keep the tone practical and matter-of-fact
EMOTION_GUIDANCE.passive: keep the tone flat and low-energy
EMOTION_GUIDANCE.urgent: sound pressed for time because work is blocked

company_wide: if it comes up at all, make it sound broader than one area without using scope labels
the requester may imply this seems to be happening in multiple places without quantifying it
multi_department: the requester may hint that people outside their immediate group are also affected
the requester may suggest the problem seems broader than just one team
single_department: the requester may hint that several coworkers in the same department, site, or office area are affected
single_team: the requester may hint that teammates nearby are running into the same thing
single_user: keep the focus mostly on the requester's own work

INTENT_GUIDANCE.ask_question: make the requester mainly ask whether this is expected or how it works
INTENT_GUIDANCE.ask_status: make the requester mainly ask for a status update
INTENT_GUIDANCE.confirm_action: make the requester confirm what they already did and ask what is next
INTENT_GUIDANCE.escalate: make the requester push for quicker attention in normal business language
INTENT_GUIDANCE.report_issue_only: make the requester mostly report the problem without proposing a fix
INTENT_GUIDANCE.request_fix: make the requester mainly want help fixing or unlocking it

INTERACTION_GUIDANCE.asked_for_more_info: write like the requester is replying with extra details
INTERACTION_GUIDANCE.following_up: write like the requester is following up
INTERACTION_GUIDANCE.no_prior_interaction: write like this is the first time the requester is reaching out about it
INTERACTION_GUIDANCE.redirected_here: hint that another team or channel redirected them to submit this here
INTERACTION_GUIDANCE.self_tried: mention one thing they already tried
INTERACTION_GUIDANCE.still_not_fixed: make it clear the issue is still not fixed

KNOWLEDGE_GUIDANCE.confused: sound unsure about what is actually wrong
KNOWLEDGE_GUIDANCE.correct_understanding: sound like the requester mostly understands the problem
KNOWLEDGE_GUIDANCE.guessing: let the requester hedge and guess about the cause
KNOWLEDGE_GUIDANCE.misdiagnosing: let the requester confidently guess the wrong cause, such as permissions vs sync delay
KNOWLEDGE_GUIDANCE.unsure_if_correct_channel: hint that the requester may not be in the right queue

business_critical: make the consequences feel urgent and operationally important without using executive jargon
show that this is creating a serious work problem without sounding like an outage report
major: show that an important task is blocked or delayed until this is resolved
make the consequences feel materially disruptive without sounding dramatic
minor: keep the consequences practical and fairly limited
moderate: make it clear this is disruptive enough to interrupt normal work
show that this is more than a small annoyance but still grounded in day-to-day work

STRUCTURE_GUIDANCE.context_first: start with background before the actual issue
STRUCTURE_GUIDANCE.follow_up: write like this is a follow-up to prior attempts, not a brand-new request
STRUCTURE_GUIDANCE.fragmented: keep it clipped, incomplete, or a little messy
STRUCTURE_GUIDANCE.narrative: describe it as a short sequence of what changed, what failed, and what is now blocked
STRUCTURE_GUIDANCE.request_first: open with the ask, then give a little context
STRUCTURE_GUIDANCE.symptom_first: open with the symptom before the explanation or ask

TEMPORAL_GUIDANCE.after_change_or_update: connect it to a recent change, setup, update, or policy/process shift
TEMPORAL_GUIDANCE.again_today: make it feel like it is happening again today
TEMPORAL_GUIDANCE.first_occurrence: if time comes up, make it feel like the first time they noticed it
TEMPORAL_GUIDANCE.recurring_issue: make it feel recurring rather than brand new
TEMPORAL_GUIDANCE.since_recent_time: anchor it to a recent time like this morning

blocked: the requester may sound stuck because their work cannot move forward
the requester may emphasize that they are unable to continue until this changes
escalated: the requester may sound sharper or more urgent after earlier attempts did not fix it
the requester may write like this has dragged on long enough and now needs quick attention
in_progress: the requester may mention that some part of this seems underway but it still is not usable
the requester may ask for completion or an update because the issue is not fully resolved yet
new_submission: write this like the requester is opening the issue for the first time
make it sound like a straightforward initial request rather than a case summary
pending_approval: the requester may be confused about why this has stalled or what is still needed
the requester may hint that they already did their part but do not know what is holding this up
pending_requester_info: the requester may be filling in details they forgot or were asked for earlier
the requester may add one or two clarifying details after earlier back-and-forth, such as date, screenshot, or reference number
triaged: the requester may assume this already reached the right place and is asking for movement
the requester may sound like they expected the owning team to pick this up already
